_desc: How to reach Salzburg by train from Vienna and Munich: journey times, the walk from the station to the old town, the best time to visit and what to see in a day.
b1: How to Get to Salzburg by Train
b2: By WoW Train · Updated October 2026 · 4 min read
b3: Baroque domes under a fortress, Mozart's birthplace, and the Alps on the horizon. Salzburg sits on the main line between Vienna and Munich, which makes it one of the easiest and most rewarding stops on a rail trip through Central Europe.
b4: What is the fastest way to get to Salzburg?
b5: From Munich, direct trains take roughly 1h 30m–1h 45m and run about hourly through the day. From Vienna, the ÖBB Railjet takes roughly 2h 30m–2h 45m, also with frequent departures. Both services arrive at Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, so you do not need to change. From Prague, Budapest or Venice, plan one change in Vienna, Munich or Villach.
b6: How to get from the station to the old town?
b7: On foot: roughly 15–25 minutes to the old town, via the Mirabell Gardens and across the river.
b8: By bus: local buses run from the station to the old town; check the live timetable.
b9: By taxi: a short ride if you are carrying luggage.
b10: When is the best time to go?
b11: Early morning. The old town is calmest before the tour groups arrive, and the fortress opens early.
b12: Late spring and early autumn have comfortable weather and fewer crowds than July and August.
b13: December brings the Christmas markets, which are beautiful but busy; book accommodation early.
b14: What to see in a day?
b15: Hohensalzburg Fortress — a funicular or a steep walk up to one of the largest medieval castles in Europe.
b16: Getreidegasse and Mozart's Birthplace — the main shopping lane and the house where Mozart was born.
b17: Salzburg Cathedral and Residenzplatz — the baroque heart of the old town.
b18: Mirabell Gardens — formal gardens close to the station, also a Sound of Music location.
b19: For a second day, Hallstatt is a classic day trip by train and ferry.
b20: You have seen it. Now go. Salzburg is on the main Vienna–Munich line: book your train and you are in the old town within half an hour of arriving. Every operator, one secure checkout.

b30: The tip worth knowing: Salzburg Hauptbahnhof is in the new town, on the north bank of the river. The old town and the fortress are on the other side, roughly 1.5 km away. Walk through the Mirabell Gardens on the way for the classic view of the fortress.
